status_note: Applies from 20 Jan 2027 (Art. 54, second paragraph). The original OJ L 165 print said 14 Jan 2027; corrigendum OJ L 169, 4.7.2023 corrected it to 20 Jan 2027. Commission and EU-OSHA pages agree. Authentic Art. 54 wording not read by hand.
clause_or_section_seen: Art. 54, second paragraph (seen in EUR-Lex consolidated text of 27.7.2026, by extraction); corrigendum OJ L 169 item 10
requirement_paraphrase: Regulation applies from 20 January 2027 (Art. 54). Notified body provisions (Arts 26 to 42, per extraction) apply from 20 January 2024. Some provisions apply from 19 July 2023, 20 July 2024 and 20 October 2026. "Directive governs until 19 January 2027" is an inference not seen in the Regulation text.
applies_to: Manufacturers placing machinery on EU market

status_note: In force; Annex III 1.1.9 text not retrieved
clause_or_section_seen: Annex III 1.1.9 (existence confirmed by Art. 20(9) cross reference; Annex text not seen)
requirement_paraphrase: Annex III section 1.1.9 exists and is cited by Art. 20(9) as covering protection against corruption (official, extraction). Its wording was not read. The five year log after upload is not confirmed anywhere in official text I could read; one unofficial reproduction places a five year tracing log in section 1.2.1 (point f), not 1.1.9, so the 1.1.9 attribution is doubtful.
applies_to: Machinery that communicates with external devices

status_note: In force; Annex III section 3 text still not retrieved from official source (2026-10-12 attempt); item numbers 3.1.1, 3.2.4, 3.3.x, 3.6.3.3 remain unverified
requirement_paraphrase: New definitions (autonomous mobile machinery, supervisor, supervisory function); control system must perform the safety functions by itself even with remote supervisory function; movement must account for risks related to the intended operating area; additions on travelling function and control-circuit failure; new section 3.6.3.3 on autonomous mobile machinery (content not given in source).

edition_or_version: Page states application 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III) and 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I)
status_note: Dates confirmed by Recital (40) of 2026/1744 and Commission news page; Art. 15 base text not seen officially. See also Art. 42(3) new.
requirement_paraphrase: High-risk AI must achieve appropriate accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity; accuracy metrics declared in instructions for use; resilience to errors and inconsistencies in the system or environment; feedback-loop mitigation for continuing-learning systems.

edition_or_version: AI Act Art. 60 as shown on unofficial reproduction; text version/amendment level not confirmed
status_note: Official: Art. 60(1)-(2) replaced by point (24): now covers Annex III and Annex I Section A systems; new Art. 60a for Section B products. The 30 day tacit approval and six month limit were not read officially.
requirement_paraphrase: Real-world testing of high-risk AI outside sandboxes requires a testing plan, market-surveillance approval (tacit after 30 days unless national law differs), registration, max about six months (one extension), informed consent, and reversibility of AI outputs; serious incidents go through Art 73.
applies_to: Providers testing high-risk AI in real conditions

edition_or_version: As published; applicability dates per site
requirement_paraphrase: Providers of high-risk AI systems must report serious incidents to market surveillance authorities: no later than 15 days after awareness (immediately once causal link established), 2 days for widespread infringements, 10 days for deaths; must investigate and not alter the system before informing authorities.
applies_to: Providers of high-risk AI systems (Annex I/III)

requirement_paraphrase: Testing must use metrics and probabilistic thresholds defined in advance and suited to the intended purpose; testing may include real-world testing, which must meet Art 57 or 60 conditions; testing is done throughout development and in any event before placing on the market or putting into service.

instrument: Regulation (EU) No 376/2014 Reporting of occurrences in civil aviation
edition_or_version: Consolidated 2018-09-11 (EUR-Lex); UK retained version also read
requirement_paraphrase: Mandatory reporting of occurrences posing significant risk by listed persons (pilot in command, designers/maintainers, ATS staff etc.) within 72 hours; organisations must have mandatory and voluntary reporting systems.
applies_to: Persons and organisations in EU civil aviation

instrument: Ruchkin et al. - Confidence Monitoring and Composition for Dynamic Assurance of Learning-Enabled Autonomous Systems
clause_or_section_seen: Approach: assumption effect analysis, assumption monitors, composition
requirement_paraphrase: Proposes runtime monitors of the assumptions behind design-time guarantees, outputting confidence, composed into a system assurance monitor; no empirical results.

edition_or_version: Guidance v1.1 (file SACE_v1_1.pdf); fetch tool reported 'July 2026'
requirement_paraphrase: Eight-stage system-level process: operating context, hazardous scenarios, safe operating concept, safety requirements, design, hazardous failures, out-of-context operation (ODM boundary and minimum risk strategy), verification; each with a GSN pattern; ML components handled via AMLAS.
applies_to: Autonomous systems in complex environments (incl. robots, drones)

instrument: SACE Safety Assurance of autonomous systems in Complex Environments
clause_or_section_seen: Eight stages; Stage 1 Activity 2 (Operational Domain Model)
requirement_paraphrase: Eight-stage process (operating context, hazardous scenarios, safe operating concept, safety requirements, design, hazardous failures, out-of-context operation, verification), each ending in a GSN pattern; the Operational Domain Model defines where safety is argued.
applies_to: Autonomous systems operating in complex environments

instrument: SACE Safety Assurance of autonomous systems in Complex Environments
requirement_paraphrase: SACE covers only the development phase before deployment; operational safety management is out of scope. Simulation is described as helping reviewers understand scenarios (Activity 3), as additional analysis to corroborate hazard validation (Activity 8), and as one option for validating the safe operating concept, including hardware-in-the-loop (Note 13); the guidance says justifying simulation representativeness is challenging.

instrument: SAE J3016 Taxonomy and Definitions for Driving Automation
requirement_paraphrase: Defines ODD as operating conditions under which a driving automation system is designed to function, including environmental, geographical and time-of-day restrictions and/or required traffic or roadway characteristics; per Note 1, rapid transient changes (e.g. inclement weather) do not necessarily represent an ODD exit.

instrument: SCSC Safety Assurance Objectives for Autonomous Systems
status_note: Published by SCSC SASWG (id 'SCSC-153' not confirmed on page)
requirement_paraphrase: Cross-domain, approach-neutral objectives for assuring autonomous systems with emphasis on ML; intentionally little on legal/regulatory requirements; excludes detailed certification-liaison considerations and organisational issues.
applies_to: Developers, safety engineers, regulators of autonomous systems

instrument: Safety Assurance Argument Templates for Autonomous Systems (Adelard for Dstl)
clause_or_section_seen: Sections 5-10 (requirements, hazard analysis, safety monitor with ML, ML sensor, performance, adaptation)
requirement_paraphrase: Provides argument templates incl. a safety-monitor architecture with environmental, health and behaviour guards, and ML-sensor arguments with confidence from real and simulated trials (headings seen); hazard analysis section suggests ODD validity/completeness could be assessed separately from hazard analysis of the intended function.
